_README: Each case asks ONE question: at the commit that introduced a publicly
documented vulnerability, would Chainwatch have fired - at commit time,
ADMISSION RULE, and it is the whole value of this file: a case may only be
added once its `parent` and `commit` have been resolved against the REAL
repository and its `source` verified against a public write-up. A case
with a guessed commit hash would produce a backtest number that looks
rigorous and means nothing, which is worse than a small corpus.
`expect.rule` is the rule that SHOULD fire. A case whose rule does not fire
is a recorded miss, not a bug to be papered over by relaxing the case - the
corpus is ground truth and is read-only in the same sense fixtures/ is
To add a case:  see BACKTEST.md, or run  python backtest.py --help

notes: Whitehat-reported via Immunefi; funds moved to treasury within 24h.
The commit replaces a one-shot constructor(name,symbol) with an
external init(address newOwner,string,string) carrying no access
control - the exact shape Rule 10 exists to catch.
Independently verified in this project: the deployed EIP-1167 clone
